core_obligations: Reduce the multiplicative statement to the more precise identity for the polynomials $P_p$ (proof lines 9005-9006).

Use the splitting principle to write down the Chern roots of $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ and to identify the Chern roots of the tensor product with the pairwise sums $x_{1,i} + x_{2,j}$ (proof lines 9006-9011).
Expand the $p$-th power of each sum by the binomial formula, whose coefficients are recovered from the shape of the polynomials $P_p$, to obtain the identity in $A^p(X)$ (proof lines 9012-9014).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the precise polynomial identity (proof lines 9005-9006).
Chern roots by the splitting principle and roots of the tensor product (proof lines 9006-9011).
Binomial expansion matched against the shape of the $P_p$ (proof lines 9012-9014).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the Chern character is multiplicative on a tensor product of finite locally free modules, together with the precise identity expressing the power sums of the Chern roots of the tensor product as a binomial combination of those of the factors (statement lines 8985-9002). The proof is an application of the splitting principle: after naming the Chern roots, those of the tensor product are the pairwise sums, and the binomial formula together with the shape of the auxiliary polynomials gives the claim. The passage through the splitting principle and the matching of the coefficients are the substance, so the claim is H2.
